scope: All 8 steps in the notebook-based raw pattern inspection example.

filters.purpose: Represent the known 32x32 square acquisition grid in micrometers. Cell centers are (column*0.25,row*0.25,0) relative to the first retained scan point. Z spacing is a 2D placeholder; no absolute specimen origin is claimed.

Read the measured-derived version 3 UP1 crop without changing detector intensities. The geometry supplies 1024 scan tuples; each tuple has 116 x 116 uint8 detector components. The version 1 row/column override is disabled.
Record local scan identity 0..1023 before cropping. X varies fastest: LocalScanIndex=row*32+column. This is not an index into detector pixels.
Recover identity in the original 500-column acquisition using row=floor(local/32) and column=local-row*32. This formula assumes the documented first 32 rows / first 32 columns crop.

Copy adjacent acquisition cells (15,15) and (16,15), inclusive, retaining every complete detector pattern and both index arrays. Keep Scan32 intact. This is a scan crop, not a crop of the 116 x 116 detector image or a phase-based selection.

Write Patterns.bin with two unchanged uint8 detector patterns (26,912 bytes, pattern then row then column). This headerless stream is not a UP1 file; use the CSV and DREAM3D checkpoint for identity and shape.

Keep both rows, including output tuple 0. Expected local indices 495,496 map to original scan indices 7515,7516. Recover original column=index%500 and row=index//500; these are acquisition indices, not detector coordinates.

Save all 1024 original cropped-scan patterns, the selected two-pattern copy, relative acquisition geometry and both identity arrays. No orientations, indexing quality, phase labels or strain measures are calculated.
